summary: This bill bars federal funds from reaching any K-12 school or college that teaches or promotes any of six listed race-based theories (such as inherent racial superiority, that the U.S. is fundamentally racist, or that individuals are responsible for others' actions because of their race) or compels students or staff to affirm them.

scores.thoughts: The bill explicitly prohibits allocation of federal funds to elementary/secondary schools and institutions of higher education that promote listed race-based theories. This directly withholds federal spending from non-compliant entities, producing a clear reduction in government outlays for education.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.
No provisions address healthcare delivery, insurance, or medical policy.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address immigration, visas, border policy, or related protections.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions address military or defense spending.
No provisions address environmental regulations or climate policy.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net benefits.

The bill conditions federal education funding on curriculum and training content in both K-12 schools and higher education institutions. It directly regulates what may be taught or promoted using public funds, producing a moderate impact on federal education policy.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance policy.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address trade, tariffs, or globalization.
By prohibiting federal funds to non-compliant schools, the bill produces a modest reduction in federal outlays that could marginally aid debt reduction efforts.
No provisions address LGBTQ protections or related legal rights.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No provisions address technology regulation or data privacy.
No provisions address labor unions, worker protections, or collective bargaining.

The bill invokes title VI of the Civil Rights Act to bar compelled affirmation of race-based theories and certain segregative practices. It therefore prioritizes enforcement of existing civil-rights anti-discrimination rules over any carve-outs, producing a modest alignment with the civil-rights end of the spectrum.
